Keyword match

Most applications are read by software first. It pulls the text out of your PDF and scores it against the words in the ad. This tab is a checklist that helps you get those words into your real sentences — nothing here is printed, exported or saved into the PDF.

Green means the word is already somewhere in your résumé. Click a grey one to drop it into a subject — then edit the sentence so it reads like you wrote it.

Uploading to a job site

Sites that say “autofill from your CV” read the PDF straight through, top to bottom. A two-column page interleaves when it is read that way — a line of your address can land in the middle of your education — which is why the boxes come back half filled or in the wrong order.

One column, ordinary headings, no icons or panels — the same content as the designed page, with nothing hidden and nothing added. Upload this one and send the designed one to the person.

Quick checks

A note on hidden text: white or 0.01 pt keywords tucked in a corner are read by the screening software exactly like normal text — it reads the text layer, not the picture — and they show up the moment anyone copies the file or opens the parsed version. Most employers treat that as a reason to bin the application. Words that are genuinely in your sentences pass both the software and the person.

How this works

1 · Pick a template

Borkin Classic is a rebuild of your existing résumé — same centred header, contact grid, two columns, grey skill panel, language bars, portfolio QR and hobby icon strip. Nineteen more are drawn from the reference designs in your two examples folders, and Playbook is built to the rules in your résumé playbook: one plain column, conventional headings, no tables, icons or skill bars — the things screening software trips over. Switching template keeps all your content.

2 · Fill in the subjects

Every subject has its own title and sub-title, and every entry inside it has a title and sub-title too. Contact rows and portfolio rows can each carry a hyperlink; portfolio rows can also show a QR code.

Every entry has its own switch, next to the move and delete buttons — and so does every bullet point. Switching one off takes it off the page but keeps the text in the project, so you can carry three versions of a job in one file and show only the one that suits the application. A switched-off entry is still editable, still movable, and never reaches the PDF.

The portfolio QR code carries the same hyperlink as the text, so it is clickable on screen and scannable on paper. You can set its colour and what sits behind it, or let the page show through. A line under the pickers reports the contrast and warns when a combination is unlikely to scan — phone cameras want dark squares on a light background, so a light code on a dark panel usually fails however good it looks.

3 · Arrange them

Drag the handle to reorder. The coloured chip moves a subject between the page's areas — main column, side column, header or footer — for templates that have them.

A couple of templates stand a narrow contact column beside the name. If what you put in the header is wider than that slot — three or more contact columns, or a block of numbers — it drops under the title and sub-title at full width instead, so the name keeps its place.

4 · Style each subject

Contact entries take only the width they need, and the leftover space is shared out evenly, so a long address is never cut off and never drops to a second line. The Spacing menu chooses between columns that line up (spread to the width, or with a fixed gap) and plain even gaps; two sliders set the space between entries and between rows. If a row would still be too wide, the block quietly shrinks a little to stay on its line.

Every subject has its own text alignment (left, centred, right or justified) and its own panel background — fill colour and opacity, text colour, corner radius, padding, border, and whether the panel merges with the page edge. The Design tab sets the defaults every panel starts from; the circular arrow next to a slider puts that one control back to the template's own value.

The Title block layout group in Content sizes and places the name, sub-title, monogram and photo — size, weight, tracking, spacing, crop, focus point, border ring, and a nudge in either direction.

5 · Export

  • Export PDF opens your browser's print dialog. Choose Save as PDF, paper A4, margins None, and tick Background graphics. This gives selectable text and clickable links.
  • Plain PDF is the one to upload where a site offers to “autofill from your CV”. Those sites read the PDF straight through, top to bottom, and a two-column page interleaves when it is read that way — which is why the boxes come back half filled. This prints the same content as one ordinary column, with plain headings and no icons or panels. Nothing is hidden and nothing is added; it is your résumé, laid out for a machine. Send the designed one to the person.
  • Download PDF saves a file immediately with no dialog. The page becomes a picture, so the text is no longer selectable or searchable — but every link, including the portfolio QR, is laid back over it and stays clickable. Handy for a quick share; for an application, prefer Export PDF, which keeps real text for the screening software to read.

6 · Come back later

Save project downloads a .resume.json file holding everything, photo included. Open loads it back. Your work is also kept in this browser automatically, so reopening this page restores your last session.

Fonts

69 families from your fonts folder are built into this file and work with no internet at all — sans, condensed, serif, mono, display, handwriting and thirteen with full Hebrew. Each is a variable font, so every weight from Light to Black comes out of one file.

Design → Your fonts → Add font files… takes any .ttf, .otf, .woff or .woff2. The family name and weight are read out of the file itself, so dropping in several weights of one family matches them up automatically. Your uploads are stored inside the saved project, so the résumé keeps its look on another machine. A font you upload with the same name as a built-in one replaces it.

Under Design → Type, section titles, entry titles, sub-titles and body text each get their own face, size, weight and colour. A single subject can override all three of those in the Content tab.

Bundled fonts come from the Google Fonts collection under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, except Roboto (Apache 2.0).

Keywords

The Keywords tab helps with the software that screens applications before a person sees them. Paste the job ad and it pulls out the words that carry meaning, or start from a suggested set for your field and add your own. Green means the word is already somewhere in your résumé; click a grey one to drop it into a subject, then edit the sentence so it reads like you wrote it. None of it is printed, exported or saved into the PDF — only what is actually on the page counts, which is the point: the parser and the person read the same document.

Keyboard

Ctrl+S save · Ctrl+P export · Ctrl+O open · Ctrl+0 zoom 100%
